entries.claim: The collect is a priestly oration after Oremus. These rubrics establish its audible delivery in a read Mass and sung delivery in a solemn or sung Mass. The prescribed conclusion and Amen are supplied by the separate RG 115 a source. These loci alone do not certify the complete response-participation map or date-specific commemoration inventory.

The Benziger 1962 Editio iuxta typicam prints the beginning of this collect on page 46 and continues it on page 47, ending with the Per Dominum cue. The continuation image and prescribed full ending have separate source uses.

The top-left continuation completes patimur across the page break and the remaining collect body through vincamus, followed by Per Dominum. It belongs to the IV Sunday collect begun on page 46 despite the later running heading.

The Father-directed formula supplies the twenty-one-word conclusion and separate Amen. Its unaccented rubric prints tuum, qui. House accents, ligatures, tuum: Qui and terminal Amen. are declared in the witness, not represented as a literal proper-page reading.
